source_commit: b1abca9a20 + uncommitted sparse .native_catalog backend swap (this handback's own change)
measurement_scope: Same harness/workload as write-amplification-vector-before.json. AFTER: sparse_backend = .native_catalog (storage/native_catalog_backend.zig, one native commit per SparseIndex.batchWithOptions publication, via sparse/sparse.zig's new .native_catalog SparseBackend/StoreOwner variant), wired through storage/lite/backend.zig's configureDbOpenOptions(ForNamespace). dense_storage_backend is UNCHANGED (.lsm): see this handback's open-risk note on hbc_adapter.zig's ~20 exhaustive switches over env_owner before HBC can safely follow sparse's lead.

dense_vector_calling_thread_syncs_per_up.note: dense stays on .lsm; small run-to-run variance (shared-machine CPU contention during this measurement), not a real regression -- see known_limitations.

known_limitations: 10.0 syncs/update for sparse is well above text's own post-WS4/WS1 target (<=1.0 at 1 writer): sparse gets WS4's FIRST milestone only (swap the LSM-on-VFS backend for one native commit per SparseIndex.batchWithOptions call) -- NOT WS1's single-fsync-manifest protocol improvement (that applies uniformly to every native commit regardless of caller) and NOT the inline-in-the-primary-commit optimization text's InlineTextPublication (WS4 phase 2) added. See this handback's Task 4 section for why an inline sparse publication was not attempted this session.

main_txn_commit shows 512 calling-thread syncs for 128 sparse updates (4/update): each update's delete-then-insert shape (deleteSparseBatchByNameWithOptions then indexSparsePreparedWritesByNameWithOptions/applySparseEmbeddingWritesByNameWithOptions) opens more than one native commit per logical write; reducing that to one commit per write is exactly the inline-publication gap above.

This measurement ran on a shared development machine with several other concurrent zig builds/tests from unrelated worktrees (confirmed via ps during the build); wall-clock writes_per_second_indicative_debug is unreliable here (see the harness's own Debug-indicative-only caveat) -- only the sync/commit/byte counts are build-mode-independent and trustworthy.
